topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: Rain taps a rhythmic tune against the window, matching the beat of the old clock ticking in the corner. I stand here, the remnants of a day's work scattered across the desk, a half-empty bottle of whiskey sitting idly by, uncleared papers whispering secrets of the past. It's the tree, you see. The one I planted. A sapling, no bigger than a promise, back when the world felt new and the hands that held the spade were a father's, strong and sure. Now it's gone, shorn from the earth as if it never took root at all. Outside, the rain keeps falling, washing away the dirt, the memories, the remnants of a boy who dreamed too big under the wrong sky.
